credentials.description: Notch Pay private key, sent as is in Authorization and in X-Grant, for transfers, beneficiaries, balance and webhooks

example_prompt: Fetch all Notch Pay beneficiaries with pagination support.

parameters.name: search
parameters.description: Optional search string to filter beneficiaries by name, email, or account number.

parameters.name: country
parameters.description: Filter by country code (Beneficiaries API page, https://developer.notchpay.co/api-reference/beneficiaries.md, GET /beneficiaries; not in the OpenAPI export).

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Filter by beneficiary type (Beneficiaries API page, https://developer.notchpay.co/api-reference/beneficiaries.md, GET /beneficiaries; not in the OpenAPI export).

totals.description: Total number of beneficiaries across all pages.

selected.description: Number of items returned in this page.

last_page.description: Last available page number. Use to detect end of pagination.

gotchas: Authorization takes the key as is, with no 'Bearer ' prefix. Which key goes there is unsettled: Notch Pay's Authentication page shows the public key in it next to X-Grant (`-H "Authorization: YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY"` `-H "X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY"`), while this spec sends the private key, following its earlier note that a public key returns 406 Not Acceptable (not stated in the docs). See open_questions before relying on either.
Query parameters (limit, page, search) must be appended to the URL as a query string — they are not sent in the request body.
When current_page equals last_page, you have reached the end of the list. Requesting beyond last_page returns an empty items array rather than an error.
Pagination uses 'totals' (not 'total') and 'selected' (not 'per_page'). Reading the wrong field name silently returns undefined.
The totals field reflects the count at the time of the request; concurrent creates or deletes can cause inconsistencies when paginating large lists.

This endpoint also requires the `X-Grant` header carrying your private key (`X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY`). Without it Notch Pay returns 403 "This endpoint requires additional authentication"; a wrong value returns 403 "Invalid grant key".
open_questions: Notch Pay's docs show `Authorization: YOUR_PUBLIC_KEY` together with `X-Grant: YOUR_PRIVATE_KEY` on this endpoint, while this spec sends the private key in Authorization (see the gotcha about 406 with a public key). Which key Authorization must carry when X-Grant is present is not confirmed.
